title: What aol.com said, 1996 to 2025
lede: The members’ service ran inside AOL’s own software and was never archived. What survives is the public website: pages the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine saved, cropped here to the page. Click one to open the original capture.[^37]

snips.text: “The World’s Most Popular Internet Online Service”
“**December 2, 1996** America Online Launches New Unlimited Use Pricing”
“AOL Anytime, Anywhere. Check Your AOL Mail.”
“AOL routinely evaluates its products and services and has decided to discontinue Dial-up Internet.”

note: We found the captures through the Wayback Machine in October 2026. The 1996 capture shows a seasonal header in Italian (“Benvenuto a”), apparently one of several rotating greetings. Some images in the 2025 capture were not archived.

captures.label: Unlimited use
captures.title: Three weeks into flat-rate pricing
captures.text: The page announces unlimited use pricing and promotes the Buddy List, “now available on AOL 3.0.” The site is a brochure for the service, with a “Try AOL” button.

captures.label: AOL.COM
captures.title: A portal beside the service
captures.text: Mail sign-in, search, shopping and “Try AOL FREE!” The top link advertises AIM 4.1. The Time Warner merger would close three months later.

captures.label: Free mail
captures.title: Six weeks after going free
captures.text: “Get Free AOL Mail,” a new logo, and search “enhanced by Google,” which had bought 5% of AOL that April.[^12]

captures.label: The day before
captures.title: A news page with a mail button
captures.text: The day before dial-up was discontinued. Nothing on the home page mentions it.
captures.warn: Several images did not load in this capture.
